catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 2 results with favorable safety
detailed_catalyst_text: The company reported first results from the Phase 2 CORE‑008 Cohort CX evaluating intravesical cretostimogene combined with gemcitabine in high‑risk non‑muscle invasive bladder cancer, including BCG‑exposed and BCG‑unresponsive patients. Data showed high-grade event-free survival at 3 and 6 months and high complete response rates in CIS-containing patients, with no grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the potential of an intravesical-only combination approach in this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: CG Oncology, Inc. (NASDAQ:CGON) today announced positive first results from CORE‑008 Cohort CX, a Phase 2 study evaluating intravesical cretostimogene grenadenorepvec in combination with gemcitabine sequential versus concurrent treatment schedules in patients with high‑risk (HR) non‑muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). As of the 2026-03-13, data cut off, the overall HG-EFS was 96.0% at 3 months and 89.5% at 6 months, with a median follow-up of 6.6 months, in the overall intent-to-treat (ITT) population. High complete response (CR) rates at any time were observed in the CIS-containing population with 85.7% (95% CI, 67.3% – 96.0%) and 92.3% (95% CI, 74.9% - 99.1%) in the ITT population with 85.7% (24/28) (95% CI, 67.3%-96.0%) and Efficacy Evaluable population with 92.3% (24/26) (95% CI, 74.9%-99.1%), respectively. A favorable safety and tolerability profile was observed with no Grade 3 or greater treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) and no deaths reported.

catalyst_text: Announced positive topline results from Phase 3 cohort
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline data from a Phase 3 cohort in high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC showed strong high-grade event-free survival at 3, 6, and 9 months with favorable safety. Enrollment was completed with no Grade 3+ treatment-related adverse events or deaths reported.
catalyst_text_evidence: CG Oncology, Inc. ... today announced topline data from BOND-003 Cohort P and first results from CORE-008 Cohort A which demonstrated promising efficacy, safety and tolerability. Results from the BOND-003 Cohort P clinical trial of cretostimogene monotherapy in patients with BCG-UR papillary-only NMIBC demonstrate encouraging HG-EFS and a consistent, well-tolerated safety profile. As of the 2025-09-01 data cut-off, in 51 efficacy evaluable patients, Kaplan-Meier estimates of HG-EFS at 3- 6- and 9-months are 95.7% (95% CI 83.8 – 98.9), 84.6% (95% CI 68.6 – 92.9%) and 80.4% (95% CI 62.3-90.4%), respectively. A favorable safety and tolerability profile was observed with no Grade 3 or greater treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) and no deaths reported. The study has completed enrollment with 56 patients receiving cretostimogene across 35 clinical sites in the United States and Japan.

catalyst_text: Reported positive initial Phase 2 results in NMIBC
detailed_catalyst_text: First results from a Phase 2 cohort in high-risk BCG-naïve NMIBC with CIS showed an overall 83.7% complete response, rising to 88.0% with optimized administration. Safety was favorable with no related serious adverse events or Grade 3+ events reported.
catalyst_text_evidence: The first results from CORE-008 Cohort A demonstrate that cretostimogene monotherapy has promising clinical efficacy, tolerability, and safety in patients with high-risk, BCG-naïve NMIBC with CIS, compared with outcomes observed in historical BCG-naive trials. As of the 2025-09-01 data cut off, the overall CR rate at any time in evaluable patients is 83.7% (41/49) (95% CI 70.3-92.7%) with the original administration achieving a 79.2% CR rate (57.8, 92.9) in 19 out of 24 patients as compared with the optimized administration which resulted in an 88.0% CR rate (68.8, 97.5) in 22 out of 25 patients. The safety and tolerability profile is consistent with prior clinical trials of cretostimogene. There are no related serious adverse events (SAEs), Grade 3+ adverse events or treatment-related discontinuations.

Data from Phase 3 was showcased at the AUA on May 5, 2024. The dosing for Phase 3 EAP began on June 18, 2024.

The final outcomes of Phase 2 will be showcased at ASCO 2024, with the abstract indicating an ITT CR rate of 57% at 12 months and 83% at any time.
